Climb the steps of Nepal's tallest pagoda temple and you pass five pairs of stone guardians. 🛕

At the bottom stand two legendary wrestlers. Above them, elephants, then lions, then griffins, and at the top two goddesses. Tradition says each pair is ten times stronger than the pair below — guarding Siddhi Lakshmi, the goddess the temple is dedicated to.

🏯 Nyatapola means "five storeys" in Newari
👑 Built in 1702 by King Bhupatindra Malla
🙏 Still standing after the 2015 earthquake that damaged so much of Bhaktapur

Our 6-day Nepal Scenic & Cultural tour spends a morning in Bhaktapur's medieval squares after a Nagarkot sunrise — private to your family or group, with a guide who knows the stories.

Which guardian would you want watching over your home? 👇

Want your family's first Himalayan sunrise? This is the gentle way to get it. 🌄

Our 9-day Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek tops out at just 3,210 m, so altitude risk is low. Walk 4–6 hours a day on well-graded trails between good teahouse villages, then climb Poon Hill before dawn to watch Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South and Machhapuchare turn gold. Back down through Ghandruk, a Gurung village. Children aged 10 and up with reasonable fitness manage it comfortably.

Private to your family, with a licensed guide, porters, teahouses, and the ACAP permit and TIMS card included.

Being fit does not protect you from altitude sickness. Going slowly does. 🏔️

This is the same briefing our guides give every trekking group:

⬆️ Above 3,000 m, raise your sleeping height by no more than about 500 m a day, with a rest day every few days
🥾 Rest days are active: hike higher, then come down to sleep
💧 Drink 3–4 litres of water a day above 3,000 m
🍺 Skip alcohol up high — it dehydrates you and hides early symptoms
🍛 Keep eating, even without appetite
⚠️ If symptoms get worse after rest, descend. No viewpoint is worth your life

This is general guidance from experienced guides, not medical advice — see your doctor before a high-altitude trek, and ask them about medication.

Every TempleFront trek is private to your group, paced with real acclimatisation days, and our guides carry a pulse oximeter.

No road reaches this lake. You fly in, then you walk. 💙

Phoksundo Lake (3,611 m) sits in Upper Dolpo, one of Nepal's most remote regions, on the Tibet border, where the ancient Bon faith lives on beside Tibetan Buddhism. On our 26-day Upper Dolpo Trek you fly Kathmandu › Nepalgunj › Juphal, reach the lake on Day 7 and spend two nights there, then cross the Kang La (5,151 m) to Shey Gompa, the Crystal Mountain.

A full camping trek, rated Very Challenging — tents, cook and crew, the restricted-area permit and a licensed guide included. Private to your group.

Stone houses stacked against the cliffs of the Manang valley. This is where the Annapurna Circuit makes you wait. 🏔️

On Day 8 of our 19-day Annapurna Circuit you walk into Manang (3,540 m). Day 9 you stay — a full acclimatisation day, hiking higher and coming back down to sleep. It is the day that makes the rest possible:

⛰️ Day 10 — Yak Kharka (4,110 m)
🌙 Day 11 — Thorong Phedi (4,600 m)
🌄 Day 12 — a 3 am start to cross the Thorong La (5,416 m), then down to Muktinath

No technical climbing, but a serious, beautiful challenge. Private to your group, with a government-licensed guide, porters, the ACAP permit and TIMS card included.
